title: The forecast is written for one monolith and has no per-service volumes
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Volume and Scale Forecast v3.xlsx
section: All eight sheets (there is no service, topic or queue anywhere)
description: Version 3 measures one Workbench: one read path, one set of scheduled jobs and one database. Arch v5 cuts Recovery into 19 services, each with its own schema, REST base, Kafka topic and Temporal task queue, so the capacity plan needs a volume per service. The source has no such split and no service owner.
evidence: v3 Read path!A2 and C15 (the Workbench reads the views; three Workbench jobs); v3 has no column named service, topic or queue on any sheet. Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 45 (own schema, topic and task queue each), line 69 (19 services, own topic and queue), line 703 (topic per service) and lines 2880 to 2898 (slide 41 service catalogue); Architecture v5 slide 48 (A8) lines 3127 to 3179 (volumes and what needs to scale); ADR-013; ADR-014; DP-01; DP-14.
proposed: A new sheet, Service volumes, gives one row for each of the 19 services with its driver, the 2027 volume taken by formula from the existing sheets, the unit, the basis cell, its topic, its task queue and its consumers; the totals on Inputs, Monthly, Five years and Route activity do not change.

title: The read path gives every Workbench screen the recovery.v_ace_* views
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Volume and Scale Forecast v3.xlsx
section: Read path (A2, C16); Inputs!G7; Key (View read)
description: Version 3 says the Workbench reads ACE through recovery.v_ace_* views and that a view read is a SELECT by a screen or by the lake refresh. Arch v5 gives the 30 views to rwb-source-data alone, read-only, and makes every other service ask it; the lake refresh no longer exists. The four cells and the Key row therefore name the wrong reader.
evidence: v3 Read path!A2 (The Workbench reads ACE through recovery.v_ace_* views), Read path!C16 (data_product_load read through v_ace_batch_status), Inputs!G7 (read through v_ace_account) and Key!C10 (a SELECT by a screen or by the lake refresh). Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 707 (only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views) and lines 1113 to 1115 (P1 SQL: SELECT recovery.v_ace_*, 30 views); ADR-010; DP-05.
proposed: The four cells and the Key row say that rwb-source-data holds the one grant and reads the views on behalf of the screens and the workflows; the headline figures of the read path do not change.

title: The three scheduled Workbench jobs include a lake refresh that the target removes
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Volume and Scale Forecast v3.xlsx
description: Version 3 counts three scheduled Workbench jobs: outbound queue dispatch, lake refresh and case list reconciliation. Arch v5 removes the data lake, retires the shared Quartz tables and runs every job as a Temporal Schedule or an event-started workflow in the owning service, so the lake refresh has no replacement and the three jobs belong to three different services.
evidence: v3 Read path!B15 and C15 (3; outbound queue dispatch, lake refresh and case list reconciliation). Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 513 (no data lake or Power BI connection, INT-19/20 removed), line 2296 (Temporal Schedules: rule promotion, measures, hash-chain check, smoke, rebalancing, WIN letters; the ACE shared Quartz tables are no longer used) and lines 2978 to 3002 (slide 44 job map: JOB-02, JOB-03, JOB-04, JOB-10); DP-10; DP-17; ADR-016.
proposed: The note names three jobs that exist in the target: case creation and allocation (JOB-02, JOB-03), reconciliation (JOB-04) and the WIN notice file (JOB-10), each a Schedule or an event-started workflow in its own service; the count of three and every figure stay as they are.

title: The forecast carries no Kafka topic, partition, retention or consumer figures
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Volume and Scale Forecast v3.xlsx
description: The source is a capacity forecast with no messaging content: no topic, partition count, replication factor, retention, record key, consumer group, retry or dead-letter setting, and no task queue. Arch v5 sets all of them, one topic and one queue per service plus the shared decision-record topic, so the document has to carry a second table that it never had. The event catalogue also names no consumer for ReportPublished.
evidence: v3 has eight sheets and none of them names a topic or a queue. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 703 (12 partitions, replication factor 3, 7 days, key caseId, CloudEvents binary, outbox and inbox, retry 1 min, 10 min, 1 h then .dlt), lines 245 to 246 (topic rwb.<name>.events.v1, task queue rwb-<name>), lines 2911 to 2963 (event catalogue) and line 1544 (tens of thousands of events a day); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 line 478 (one queue per service, 19) and line 520 (namespace rwb-recovery, KEDA on backlog); ADR-015; ADR-016; DP-09; DP-14.
proposed: A new sheet, Topics and queues, lists the 19 service topics and the shared rwb.decision-record.v1 with partitions, replication, retention, record key, consumer groups, retry and dead letter, then the 19 task queues with their workflows, activities and Schedules, then the platform settings; the missing consumer of ReportPublished is carried as the placeholder.

title: No demand figure exists for payments, guarantee claims, partner instructions, the report read volume, the lots or the deviation share
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Volume and Scale Forecast v3.xlsx
description: Several services own a driver that the forecast never counts. There is no payment count (rwb-payment), no guarantee or insurance claim count (rwb-guarantee), no partner instruction or result count (rwb-partner), no dashboard or report read count (rwb-reporting), no number of debt-sale lots (only accounts sold) and no share of cases that raise a deviation (rwb-deviation). Their per-service volumes cannot be calculated from the source without inventing one.
evidence: v3 Inputs rows I01 to I34 and Route activity rows 5 to 9 contain no such figure; the source counts cases, documents, interactions, decisions, rule evaluations, lawsuits, repossessions, letters, NPA sales, debt-sale accounts and users only. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 lines 1236 to 1250 (P8 and S9 contracts), lines 1322 to 1332 (S3), lines 1397 to 1408 (S6 lots) and lines 1057 to 1063 (S8 screening).
proposed: The row carries the §R9 placeholder instead of a figure, and the basis column states what the source does give: the run cadence (one per business day), the lot-based cadence, or the named stock.

title: Arch v5 states 3,110 new cases a month; the forecast divides the account inflow by 1.2
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Volume and Scale Forecast v3.xlsx
section: Inputs (I08 to I11); Monthly (column C); Five years (column C)
description: Arch v5 slide 48 and its notes state about 3,110 new cases a month, 64-74k documents a month and 283-318k rule evaluations a month. The forecast divides new accounts by the accounts-per-case assumption of 1.2, which gives about 2,980 cases a month, so its documents sit inside the slide's range while its decision entries and rule evaluations run slightly above it. The two sources do not agree on the case inflow.
evidence: v3 Inputs!I08 (accounts per case 1.2), Monthly!C5 (new accounts divided by Inputs!C12) and Five years!C5. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 line 2433 (about 23,600 open cases today, 47,389 by 2031; 64-74k documents a month; 283-318k rule evaluations a month) and lines 3131 to 3144 (3,110 new cases a month; 64-74k; 283-318k). R-PREC ranks the Arch v5 narrative above the data documents, but the forecast is the one artefact that holds the drivers.
proposed: The forecast keeps its own formula and its own figures; the per-service rows and the cross-check block cite the slide 48 figure and state that it is rounded up, so a reader sees both numbers in one place.

title: Three scheduled Workbench jobs in the forecast against 21 jobs in the Arch v5 job map
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Volume and Scale Forecast v3.xlsx
description: Version 3 counts three scheduled Workbench jobs. The Arch v5 job map runs JOB-02 to JOB-22 across the platform and the services, of which JOB-05 is retired; the two counts describe different things (jobs inside the Workbench then, jobs across 19 services and Airflow now) and the forecast does not say which scope its three belong to.
evidence: v3 Read path!B15 (3) and C15. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 lines 2978 to 2997 (slide 44 job map, JOB-02 to JOB-22, JOB-05 retired, JOB-11 in every service, JOB-21 and JOB-22 on the platform), line 2296 and lines 3002 (each job in its owning service; Airflow owns only the cross-system edges).
proposed: The count of three stays as the number of Workbench-side jobs of v3, and the note names which three they are in the target; the full job map stays in the Batch and Scheduling and Temporal catalogues.
